campaign: Overgo-native automation, orchestration control plane, and operator workbench
doctrine: Follow skill.md. LocalAI is a behavior inventory only: do not copy its source, assets, schemas, dependencies, route shapes, mutable stores, schedulers, backend loaders, or frontend framework into Overgo. Implement every capability through Overgo's existing owners before creating a new common component. Recipe and workflowcontract own immutable intent and topology; workflowruntime owns stage execution; operation owns admission, cancellation, recovery, and live lifecycle; runrecord and OvergoDB own immutable lineage, decisions, observations, and active aliases; capabilityruntime and modelrecipe own residency, peer compatibility, and remote execution; agenttool owns effect classification and authorization; server owns protocol projections and the embedded GUI. No second operation manager, workflow graph, scheduler, trace store, agent store, vector authority, peer registry, frontend state authority, or direct executor path. A new shared component must be proven by the first production vertical before a second consumer adopts it. GUI forms consume server-published typed metadata; lifecycle updates use the existing SSE stream, never per-page polling. Outbound delivery, remote media, and administrative mutations are effect-classified operations with explicit policy and durable decisions. Peer identity is per-peer and capability-bound; a shared enrollment secret never authorizes steady-state mutation. Placement, retry, retention, schedule, replica, latency, resource, and display policies derive from recipes, requests, resource plans, or recorded evidence. Each slice migrates every caller and deletes displaced construction or local state in the same commit. After every gated implementation commit, merge master, preserve master's concurrent GUI work through the common owners, rerun the affected gate, and redispatch. Completion requires real manual and scheduled automation, one remote whole-model placement vertical, API and GUI access, restart recovery, bounded evidence projections, browser validation, race validation, zero LocalAI runtime or source dependency, and no duplicate orchestration authority. Multi-user tenancy, arbitrary backend galleries, biometrics, and a React migration are explicitly outside this campaign.

items.title: Establish immutable automation authority and compile it into existing workflow plans

steps.title: Define and publish automation definitions, trigger and delivery policy identities, active aliases, and bounded RepoDB queries through existing recipe and run-record owners
steps.verify: rg -q 'func TestAutomationDefinition' internal && rg -q 'func TestAutomationActivation' internal && go test ./internal/recipe ./internal/workflowcontract ./internal/runrecord -run 'TestAutomationDefinition|TestAutomationActivation' -count=1
steps.rationale: Automation needs one immutable source of truth before runtime or GUI work. Definitions reference existing recipe, model, dataset, capability-bundle, trigger-policy, and delivery-policy artifacts instead of embedding mutable configuration or creating another store.

steps.title: Compile the active automation definition into a deterministic AutomationExecutionPlan over the existing recipe graph, operation policy, resources, triggers, and deliveries
steps.rationale: Runtime must receive one complete, immutable plan and hard-fail missing aliases, incompatible recipes, unsupported triggers, unapproved deliveries, stale artifacts, or incomplete resource authority. Direct construction paths are prohibited.

items.title: Execute manual and scheduled automation through common operation and workflow owners

steps.title: Run one active automation end to end through operation admission, workflowruntime stages, stage receipts, durable outputs, cancellation, and restart recovery
steps.rationale: This is the first production vertical and proves the common authority without a second job runner. Every run reuses the existing operation identity, stage receipts, human decisions, attempts, and artifact lineage.

steps.title: Add recipe-owned schedule triggers with a single durable claim, injectable clock, missed-run policy, and duplicate-fire refusal
steps.rationale: Scheduling is orchestration, not a parallel runtime. Schedule parsing and due-time calculation belong to the typed trigger contract; claims and outcomes belong to OvergoDB; execution remains an ordinary operation. Timing and catch-up behavior come from policy identities, not literals.

steps.title: Deliver automation outputs only through effect-classified tools with allowlisted destinations, approval recovery, attempt evidence, and idempotency identity
steps.rationale: Webhook-style delivery is useful but must not become an unrestricted HTTP side door. Existing tool manuals, effect classes, decisions, operations, and serving observations provide the reusable safety and evidence path.

items.title: Prove common route, schema-form, and lifecycle components with the automation workspace

steps.title: Replace duplicated navigation and capability checks with one server-owned workspace manifest consumed by the embedded modular GUI
steps.rationale: Overgo should retain its dependency-light embedded GUI, but list/detail/editor routes, visibility, capability gates, and active navigation need one owner before orchestration expands. This does not authorize a framework migration.

steps.title: Publish typed field metadata and implement one reusable form renderer with identities, enums, units, constraints, applicability, validation, and unsaved-change protection
steps.rationale: The automation editor is the proving consumer. Metadata is projected from Go contracts; the browser must not duplicate defaults, limits, enum lists, model facts, or policy constants. A second consumer is forbidden until this vertical is working.

steps.title: Expose automation inventory, definition editing, activation, manual execution, schedules, deliveries, run history, cancellation, decisions, outputs, and refusal reasons through API and GUI
steps.rationale: The UI is a projection and control surface over authoritative contracts and existing runtime operations. It must deep-link definitions, recipes, operations, attempts, decisions, stage receipts, artifacts, and deliveries without owning hidden state.

items.title: Make operation and serving evidence globally visible without a second trace authority

steps.title: Add bounded projected queries and summaries over operations, stage receipts, serving observations, interactions, resources, and decisions
steps.rationale: Overgo already records the authoritative facts. The missing capability is a bounded join and summary projection, not another mutable trace buffer or copied request/response database. Heavy or sensitive payloads remain artifact references and require explicit retrieval.

steps.title: Add a persistent global operation strip and route-addressable detail view for progress, blocked decisions, cancellation, recovery, failures, attempts, resources, outputs, and trace links
steps.rationale: Long-running work must remain visible across navigation. The shell consumes the existing SSE stream and durable operation state; it never polls, infers cancellation client-side, or maintains a browser-only terminal history.

items.title: Turn remote peer capability facts into an identity-bound whole-model serving control plane

steps.title: Add per-peer enrollment identity, approval, capability publication, heartbeat leases, administrative states, drain and retirement authority to RepoDB
steps.rationale: The existing remote peer authority proves compatibility for one request but does not own node lifecycle. Steady-state mutations must authenticate the enrolled peer identity and bind every capability update and heartbeat to it; a shared enrollment credential is insufficient.

steps.title: Compile deterministic whole-model placement and replica plans from active recipes, peer compatibility, artifact locality, residency, observed resources, and requested service policy
steps.rationale: Eligibility precedes ranking. The compiler must explain admission and refusal, preserve exact artifact and recipe identities, and derive replica and resource decisions without endpoint-order fallback or hard-coded VRAM thresholds.

steps.title: Reconcile placement plans through existing operations with artifact staging, load, zero-active-lease unload, drain completion, retry evidence, and restart recovery
steps.rationale: The first distributed target is horizontal whole-model serving, not layer sharding. Reconciliation uses the existing operation manager and session director; it must not introduce a second job queue or evict active sessions.

items.title: Expose peer lifecycle, placement, capacity, and evidence through the common operator workbench

steps.title: Add typed peer inventory, enrollment, approval, heartbeat, drain, placement, reconciliation, capacity, artifact, attempt, and log projections
steps.rationale: Endpoints project existing peer, placement, operation, session, and serving evidence. They do not become a mutable registry and must enforce administrative versus peer-scoped capabilities explicitly.

steps.title: Add peer inventory, detail, capacity, labels, placement rules, staging progress, drain controls, attempts, refusal explanations, and logs using the common manifest, forms, operation shell, and SSE stream
steps.rationale: This is the second consumer that validates the common workspace components. It must reuse schema forms and operation views rather than cloning LocalAI's node UI, adding a peer-specific poller, or embedding placement constants.

items.title: Build durable agent configuration and retrieval on automation, dataset, capability-bundle, and interaction owners

steps.title: Add immutable agent definitions and active aliases referencing prompt, model recipe, tool manuals, capability bundles, datasets, automation definitions, and policy identities
steps.rationale: The current agent endpoint coordinates a session and registered tools but does not own durable agent configuration. Definitions compose existing authorities; they do not create a filesystem skill store, arbitrary plugin loader, or mutable personality object.

steps.title: Add dataset-derived chunk and embedding identities plus a rebuildable retrieval index projection with citations, reranking, and exact lineage
steps.rationale: RepoDB remains authority for datasets, chunks, embedding recipes, and lineage; the similarity index is a derived cache that can be rebuilt. Existing embedding and reranking capabilities are reused instead of adding a second vector database or RAG store.

steps.title: Expose agent inventory, typed editing, activation, pause and resume, chat, automation attachment, retrieval evidence, tools, decisions, and structured observables through API and GUI
steps.rationale: The UI shows structured lifecycle, tool, retrieval, decision, and artifact events—not hidden model reasoning. It reuses the workspace manifest, schema form, operation shell, interaction ledger, and automation runtime.

items.title: Validate production orchestration, browser behavior, recovery, concurrency, and ownership closure

steps.title: Run real manual and scheduled automation plus remote whole-model placement through active authority, API, GUI projections, operations, restart recovery, and evidence publication
steps.rationale: Mocks can prove contracts but cannot close the capability campaign. The final verticals must use active definitions and aliases, actual RepoDB persistence, existing operation/workflow owners, one enrolled remote peer, and exact lineage from request to output.

steps.title: Add and run an Overgo-owned browser acceptance lane for routing, narrow and desktop layouts, schema forms, unsaved changes, SSE progress, decisions, cancellation, recovery, and accessibility semantics
steps.rationale: Static asset tests do not prove browser interaction. The lane is an Overgo test tool, not LocalAI frontend code or a production runtime dependency, and it must fail rather than silently skip when a changed GUI surface lacks its browser prerequisite.

steps.title: Prove concurrency and restart safety, remove displaced constructors and local state, verify common-component reuse, and close LocalAI and magic dependency surfaces
steps.verify: go test ./... -count=1 && go vet ./... && go run ./cmd/race-lane && go run ./cmd/closure-scan -check-all -require-no-stale -require-no-uncatalogued-production -require-no-policy-copies -require-no-model-facts && ! rg -n -i 'localai|github.com/mudler/localai' -- go.mod go.sum internal cmd scripts
steps.rationale: Completion is behavioral and structural: one authority per fact, one lifecycle owner, one scheduler path, one route/schema/form system, one operation stream, no browser-only truth, no direct automation or peer executor, no copied LocalAI implementation, and no new unexplained policy literals.
